content: The Far Eastern University Institute of Nursing is recognized as one of the leading nursing schools in the Philippines, excelling in board licensure performance and the successful employment of its graduates in various nursing settings. The institute offers a Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) program, which qualifies graduates to take the Philippine Board Licensure Examination. Additionally, its Master of Arts in Nursing (MAN) program is considered one of the best in the Philippines and across Asia. Under the leadership of its current dean, Annabelle R. Borromeo, CNS, the institute has implemented strict student selection and retention policies, invested in advanced technology, and employed a faculty with master’s-level qualifications. These efforts have positioned the FEU Institute of Nursing as a driving force in both nursing education and practice in the Philippines. The Institute of Nursing was established in 1955, initially offering a three-year diploma program leading to a Graduate in Nursing (GN) qualification. Teofista G. Villarica served as its first principal. Later, a two-year Advanced Professional Program was introduced to provide GN graduates with opportunities to expand their knowledge and appreciation of the nursing profession. Lucrecia Llanera was the first directress of this program. By 1960, Felicidad D. Elegado was appointed principal of both programs, and the School of Nursing was elevated to the status of an Institute, with Elegado as its first dean. The curriculum was upgraded from a three-year course to a five-year baccalaureate program, culminating in a BSN degree. In 1978, upon Dean Elegado’s retirement, Lydia A. Palaypay assumed the deanship. Under her leadership, the five-year program was revised into a four-year BSN curriculum, which became more competency-based and community health-centered, aligning with the needs of contemporary Philippine society. This reoriented curriculum contributed to the institute’s near-perfect passing rates in licensure examinations. When Dean Palaypay was appointed Vice President for Academic Affairs in 1994, Prof. Norma M. Dumadag took over as dean. During her tenure, the institute achieved Level II PAASCU accreditation and reconfigured the BSN curriculum to include two years of Associate in Health Science Education (ASHE). The consistent high performance of its graduates in licensure exams led to the institute being certified to offer a master’s degree in nursing starting in the 2002-2003 academic year. Graduates of the FEU Institute of Nursing hold key positions in prominent health institutions in the Philippines, such as the UP-PGH, St. Luke’s Medical Center, Makati Medical Center, National Kidney Center, and the Philippine Heart Center. Many also work abroad in countries like the United States, Canada, Europe, and the Middle East. Dean Annabelle Reyes Borromeo, RN, PhD, CCRN, CNS, CPAN, obtained her basic nursing degree from the UP-PGH School of Nursing. She earned her Master of Science in Nursing from the University of Texas Health Science Center in Houston and her PhD in Nursing with a minor in statistics from Texas Woman’s University. She has extensive experience in critical care nursing and holds certifications in critical care and post-anesthesia nursing. She is also a licensed Clinical Nurse Specialist in Texas and the Philippines and a member of the prestigious Sigma Theta Tau honor society for nursing. Dean Borromeo has received numerous honors and awards, authored books, and published articles in journals and magazines. Her most recent article, published in Newsbreak, discussed the decline of nursing education in the Philippines. She has been listed in Who’s Who in American Nursing and Who’s Who in American Nursing Education since 1993. After working in the United States for 30 years, she returned to the Philippines in 2000 to contribute to her home country. She became the first Chief Nursing Officer of the Asian Hospital and Medical Center in Alabang, Muntinlupa, and currently serves as a Senior Consultant for her consulting firm, assisting hospitals with organizational development and helping students pass licensure exams. She is also a Quality Consultant for the Joint Commission on International Accreditation (JCIA) and the Dean of the FEU Institute of Nursing. Dean Borromeo is married to Dr. Andy Borromeo, an orthopedic surgeon, and they have one son, Andrew. Her mission is to teach, motivate, and inspire. The vision of the FEU Institute of Nursing is to become the preferred nursing school within five years, producing graduates who can practice independently in any setting, not solely focusing on employment as the primary career opportunity. The institute aims to develop competent, God-fearing, and socially responsive nurses who can address the changing needs of society at local, national, and international levels. It is committed to providing quality education through a competency-based, community health-centered curriculum, complemented by co-curricular and extracurricular activities of socio-cultural and spiritual nature. The institute offers academic programs such as the Associate in Health Science Education, leading to Nursing, Medical Technology, and Physical Therapy; the Bachelor of Science in Nursing; and the Master of Arts in Nursing. Students undergo training in affiliated hospitals, supervised by qualified clinical instructors, where they apply nursing theories in real-world care delivery. The FEU Institute of Nursing is also home to the Virtual Integrated Nursing Education Simulation Laboratory (VINES), the first of its kind in the Philippines. This state-of-the-art simulated hospital meets international standards, including those of the Joint Commission, and features advanced nurse call systems in partnership with Austco. This system trains students to respond to patient calls within two minutes, enhancing their customer service and interpersonal skills.
